posts.topic: making a family tornado plan everyone actually knows
posts.caption:
The best family plan is one every person can explain, even the youngest. Pick your spot, decide who helps who, and walk through it together once so it feels familiar. An above-ground shelter means no stairs in that walk-through, which keeps the plan simple for everyone. Learn more at steelhavenshelters.com.

#FamilyPreparedness #StormSafety #SteelHavenShelters #HomePreparedness

posts.topic: why a shelter steps from your door matters when warnings are short
posts.caption:
When a warning gives you only a short window, a short walk makes a real difference. Steel Haven shelters can sit in a garage or on a slab close to the house, so your family's path is quick and familiar. Walls and ceiling are 1/4-inch solid steel plate with fully welded seams. Have questions about placement? Call us at (731) 207-0868.

posts.topic: the fall tornado season in the Mid-South and Southeast
posts.caption:
November is a good, quiet time to think through your storm plan across the Mid-South and Southeast. If a shelter is on your list, start with the foundation. Ours install on a concrete slab at least 4 inches thick, and anchoring to the slab is the customer's responsibility. Getting the slab sorted early keeps the rest of the process simple. Ask about financing through Synchrony at steelhavenshelters.com.

#StormPreparedness #FamilySafety #SteelHavenShelters #StormProtection

posts.topic: nighttime tornadoes and how to make sure warnings wake you up
posts.caption:
A good night-time plan starts before bedtime. Turn on emergency alerts on your phone, keep it charged near the bed, and make sure everyone knows where you'll meet. Once you're inside the shelter, the door locks from the interior and the space has ventilation, so your family can settle in calmly. Questions about a plan that fits your home? Call us at (731) 207-0868.

posts.topic: weather radios and alert apps — set them up before you need them
posts.caption:
Set up your weather radio and alert apps on a calm afternoon, not in a hurry. Add fresh batteries, choose alerts for your county, and test them so they feel familiar. Then you can count on a quiet, steady heads-up, and your family can head to a shelter with a standard 4 ft x 6 ft interior and 6 ft of height. Take a look at the details at steelhavenshelters.com.

#WeatherRadio #StormPreparedness #FamilyPreparedness #SteelHavenShelters

posts.topic: practicing a shelter drill with kids so it feels routine, not scary
posts.caption:
Make a shelter drill feel like any other family routine: calm, simple, and done together. Let the kids lead the way to the door, talk through where everyone will sit, then head back to whatever you were doing. A few relaxed practice runs help the plan feel familiar instead of scary. We serve families across 17 states in the Midwest and Southeast, and you can see if that includes yours at steelhavenshelters.com.
